dedupe_keys.name: dataset of cyber induced mechanical faults on buildings with network and buildings data nrel

description: This National Renewable Energy Laboratory dataset records what happens inside a building when a rogue device on the building automation network sends false commands. A DOE reference building model was run in Alfalfa, which exposes the simulation as if it were a live building, and a building automation system sent BACnet control commands to simulated devices such as dampers while an attacker disrupted the network. Both the network traffic and the physical building data were logged so that a mechanical fault can be traced back to its network source. The release has a metadata file describing the scenarios, eight attack scenario archives (the first two about 27 MB each) and three baselines for summer, winter and shoulder seasons. Coverage: one simulated US reference building. Access: free download of 12 files from the NLR (formerly NREL) Data Catalog; the OSTI record gives doi:10.7799/1922641. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): NLR data catalogue licence (Alliance for Energy Innovation terms: use with attribution and disclaimer). Caveats: the building is simulated, not measured, and the attacks come from one threat model, a rogue device. Simulation uses are training and testing fault detection that joins cyber and physical signals, and checking how control attacks spread to comfort and energy use in building digital twins. Related records: DOE commercial reference buildings, BACnet packet captures and the KNXnet/IP intrusion dataset.
